gupta-review-question: Section 3, p.6: the review question, framed with SPICE, is stated verbatim by the authors.
gupta-review-registration: Section 3, p.6: PRISMA, PROSPERO ID CRD42024562024 and Covidence stated as the review's own method.
gupta-search-period: Section 3, p.6: after-2015 limit, the 10 May to 10 June 2024 searches and the adaptation to Embase, Scopus, arXiv and IEEE are all stated in the search-strategy paragraph.
gupta-eligible-qml-hardware: Abstract, p.1: the inclusion criterion is stated by the authors for their own review.
gupta-ehr-proxy-scope: Section 3, p.8: the proxy-data rule and the clinical-notes exclusion are stated as the review's own scope.
gupta-screening-process: Section 3, p.9, Screening paragraph: two screeners (health and physics), three full-text reviewers, conflicts by discussion or a third reviewer.
gupta-quality-appraisal-scope: Section 3, p.9: the appraisal scope (rigor of QML investigation, no clinical robustness) and the two-reviewer max-score rule are stated by the authors.
gupta-exclusion-rule-two-zero-scores: Appendix F, p.29, template field 17 (Judgement): 'Do not proceed if at least two scores from Q1, Q2, Q3, or Q4 is zero. EXCLUDE STUDY'. Checked on the rendered page.
gupta-synthesis-requires-noise: Appendix F, p.29, field 29 'For synthesis?': 'Must use hardware or discuss / simulate the affect of noise'. The template layout is terse (two options in one Boolean field), but Section 4.1 and Fig. 5(a) agree: 30 ideal-simulation-only studies were dropped before the 16 synthesized.
gupta-borderline-definition: Section 4.1, p.11: the paper defines 'borderline' in its own words with the three concerns listed.
gupta-quantum-advantage-definition: Section 1, p.2: the paper defines both terms (asymptotic and empirical quantum advantage) as the meaning it uses.
gupta-qml-scope-classical-data: Section 2, p.3: 'For the scope of this review' the input is a classical dataset; stated as the review's own scope.
gupta-linear-quantum-model-definition: Section 2.1, p.4: the paper defines linear quantum models and states what 'linear' refers to (linearity in the embedding).
gupta-physics-studies-without-health-set: Section 4.1, p.9: the authors state that physics-centric QML studies without an explicit health setting are not returned by the search or screening. A limit of their own search.
qmlhealth-screening-counts: Counts of the review's own screening, stated in Abstract p.1 and Section 4.1 p.9 and drawn in Fig. 5(a), p.10 (4915 screened, 313 full text, 169 extracted, 123 low quality, 46 assessed, 30 ideal-simulation-only, 16 synthesized). 169-123=46 and 46-30=16 agree. Counts of the review's own procedure, not a measured effect. The reader's flag on other counts (EHR and hardware numbers in Intro, Section 5, Fig. 7) does not touch these.
gurobi-mipgap-default-range: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. MIPGap and MIPGapAbs entries give type, default and range; checked in the text.
gurobi-mipgap-mip-only: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. Both the MIPGap and the MIPGapAbs entries carry the note 'Only affects mixed integer programming (MIP) models'.
gurobi-improvestartgap: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. ImproveStartGap entry, including the 0.1 example, as written.
gurobi-tunetargetmipgap: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. TuneTargetMIPGap entry: stop-at-target and the TuneCriterion condition are stated.
gurobi-poolgap: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. PoolGap and PoolGapAbs entries with the 100 to 120 example.
gurobi-bestbdstop-tolerance-note: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. BestBdStop entry: termination rule, USER_OBJ_LIMIT status and the tolerance warning.
gurobi-integrality-tolerance: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. IntFeasTol definition is in its entry. The 1e-5 binary and trickle-flow sentences are in the IntegralityFocus entry (same page), which the value merges; the content is accurate.
gurobi-timelimit-overrun: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. TimeLimit entry: the Runtime-may-exceed-TimeLimit note is in the entry.
gurobi-worklimit-deterministic: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. WorkLimit entry. 'Very roughly one second' is the page's own hedged statement.
gurobi-seed-perturbation: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. Seed entry describes what the parameter does.
gurobi-concurrent-mip-nondeterministic: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. ConcurrentMIP entry states the non-determinism.
gurobi-threads-default: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. Threads entry: default 0, the 32-thread soft limit and -1 are all stated.
gurobi-nonconvex-spatial-branching: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. NonConvex entry, setting 2 and the default -1 as written.
gurobi-function-constraints-deprecated: Vendor documentation of its own product (Gurobi 13.0), a parameter definition as the page states it. Deprecation note appears in the FuncPieceError entry and the related Func* entries.
gurobi-page-version-date: Page footer: 'Last updated on Oct 09, 2026', as written.
gurobi-mipgap-relative-gap-definition: The reader's value matches the MIPGap and MIPGapAbs entries: gap = |z_P - z_D|/|z_P|, zero when both are zero, infinity when z_P=0 and z_D not, opposite-sign behavior, and the MIPGapAbs rule. The stored value is narrower and drops the zero and infinity cases. Vendor definition of its own parameter, not a performance claim.
qfl-contribution-two-poc: Section I.B, pp.1-2: the paper states its own contributions (overview and two PoC simulations).
qfl-definition-qfl: Section I, p.1: the paper defines QFL in its own words.
qfl-hybrid-data-encoding-setting: Section I, p.1: the 'ideal' quantum-data setting and the hybrid setting are described as the paper's framing.
qfl-three-encodings-defined: Section II.A, pp.2-3: vanilla, mean and half are defined as used in the paper's designs. The paper later contradicts itself on which encoding performs best (Section VI.C, pp.6-7), but that does not touch the definitions.
qfl-poc-setup-poc1: Section VI.A-B, p.6: PennyLane variational classifier, IRIS dataset, simulated federation, default.qubit device, n devices trained, accuracy averaged. All as stated.
qfl-poc-setup-poc2: Section VI.A, p.6: JAX tensor circuits, MNIST shared with 3 classes per device, resizing, local training, server parameter averaging over communication rounds. All as stated.
surrogate-method-description: Abstract, p.1: the authors' own statement of their method.
surrogate-line-search-procedure: Section II, p.2: the procedure as the authors describe it (conjugate directions from the surrogate Hessian, grid of N shifts, polynomial fit, Hessian held fixed).
surrogate-sws-truncation: Section II, p.2: NMAX and NCUT truncation of the sparse wave function simulator, and sampling noise as an option, as stated.
surrogate-sampling-noise-is-gaussian: Appendix A, p.8: the authors' own simulation of sampling noise is Gaussian shifts to the energies, not shot noise from a circuit. The 'no noticeable effect' remark is the authors' reason for their design choice. A property of the setup, not evidence about hardware noise.
surrogate-models-studied: Section II, p.3 and Table I: the molecules, bases, H4 distance and TFIM parameters match.
surrogate-powell-baseline-setup: Section III, p.3: Powell and line search both start from the surrogate parameters, and Powell's initial directions come from the surrogate Hessian. This favors Powell, which bears on the outperformance claim, not on this setup statement.
surrogate-noise-levels-studied: Section III, p.3: the three error-bar levels are stated as the experimental design.
surrogate-simultaneous-update-limit: Section III, pp.4-5: the authors say the energy can increase because all directions are updated at once (seen in the N2 example), and propose sequential updates as future work. Stated limit of their own result; result type should be limit rather than claim.
surrogate-tfim-small-bond-dimension: Appendix E.2, p.12: the authors say the ansatz is classically tractable at bond dimension 100 and that the bond dimension of 4 is artificially small, chosen for a proof of principle. A limit of the hardware demonstration, stated by them.
surrogate-qpu-ansatz-symmetry: Appendix E.2, p.12: all identical operators in parallel share one angle. The remark on sampling overhead is the authors' design rationale, stated with 'may'.
surrogate-qpu-energy-runs: Appendix E.3, p.15: dates, four identical runs targeted at 8192 shots, error bars of one standard deviation, as stated.
surrogate-line-search-algorithm-appendix: Appendix B, p.9: the algorithm as the authors describe it, including 1+(M-1)Ndir points and the cubic-to-quartic fit.
surrogate-negative-eigenvalue-limit: Section V, p.6: the authors state that negative Hessian eigenvalues make the line search struggle. Their own limit; Appendix E.2 p.14 shows a negative eigenvalue (-8.26) leading to truncation.
surrogate-open-problem-truncate-bad-dire: Section V, p.7: the authors state the open problem of ill-defined Hessian directions in their own method.
gustafson-hessian-dependence-limit: Section V, p.6 (the quote sits on p.6 of the text, not p.7): the efficacy of the line search depends on accurate conjugate directions from the low-level Hessian. The limit is the authors' own and Section III p.5 shows it (N2 with NCUT below 300 gives an ill-defined Hessian).
hqnn-problem-objective: Section II, p.2: objective and earthquake focus stated by the authors.
hqnn-graph-size: Section II B, p.2: 357 nodes, 549 edges, degrees 2 to 5, three exit points, as stated.
hqnn-travel-time-sampling: Section II B, p.2: Gaussian sampling around a nominal travel time, as stated.
hqnn-instance-generation: Section II B, p.2: random epicenter, random start, one of three exits per instance.
hqnn-three-weight-mechanisms: Section II C, p.3: three mechanisms, Algorithm 1 and the 'shorter distance, stronger increase' rule.
hqnn-nodewise-dijkstra-definition: Section I, p.1: the paper defines the term for its baseline.
hqnn-training-labels: Section III, p.4: labels from node-wise Dijkstra, as stated.
hqnn-input-vector: Section III A, p.5: 6 + 5x6 = 36 values with zero padding; Table II lists main 34 plus FiLM 2.
hqnn-heuristic-global-features: Section III A, p.4: Euclidean and cosine distances added per adjacent edge, as stated.
hqnn-arrival-rate-definition: Section III B, p.5: the metric defined with its formula.
hqnn-accuracy-definition: Section III B, p.5: the metric defined with its formula.
hqnn-phn-architecture: Section III C, p.6: PHN of a classical NN and a VQC, parallel information flow in the FiLM submodels, as stated.
hqnn-film-qubit-section: Section III C, p.6: two FiLM qubits, Pauli Z data reuploading, five repeats, BEL with four sub-layers. Table II lists 'Number of Repeats 1' without saying what it repeats; no conflict is shown.
hqnn-main-qubit-section: Section III C, p.7: five-qubit QDIL, computational-basis measurement, 5 expectation values.
hqnn-classical-branch-and-combination: Section III C, p.7 and Table II: three FC layers, 36 inputs, 100 hidden, ReLU, dropout 0.5, five outputs, concatenation to ten then five.
hqnn-trained-on-simulator: Section III C p.7 and Section IV B 2 p.9: trained on the QMware simulator, as stated.
hqnn-table-ii-hyperparameters: Section III C, p.6: the text points to Table II, which is on p.7 and lists the hyperparameters.
hqnn-fisher-setup: Section IV C 3, p.12: 20 Gaussian feature samples, targets over 3-qubit basis states, 20 weight realizations in [0, 2 pi).
hqnn-qubit-setup: Fig. 3 caption, p.6: seven qubits, five main and two FiLM; Table II p.7 also says 7.
single-city-graph-scope: Abstract p.1 and Conclusion p.13 (not p.10): tested on hypothetical situations on one concrete city graph; the authors say future research must test different and larger graphs. Their own limit.

theory_low.hqnn-zx-redundant-parameter: A result on one small example circuit (Fig. 7), asserted in one sentence ('self-annihilates with its adjoint'), not proved for the circuit and not shown beyond the figure. The paper itself says only that the larger circuit 'might include some redundancies'.
